messages:
Aisha K.: FYI — Pavo (prospect) wants to run a short POC on a finetuned Llama30b variant for entity extraction. They want hosted API first, but may need Dedicated if throughput/latency doesn't meet their SLA. Can we do a quick variant compatibility + pricing sketch? cc @Tom L., @Riley M.

Tom L.: Quick clarifying q's: 1) Is the variant using a custom tokenizer? 2) Any PII/sensitive data that forces Private deployment? 3) Expected sustained QPS / peak concurrency?

Aisha K.: Not custom tokenizer — it's standard llama-tokenizer. There will be PHI in some tests, so they asked about Private + KMS, but early POC can be hosted with data obfuscation. Estimated baseline: 25 qps sustained, bursts to 150 for 30s. Latency goal ~ < 400ms p50.

Riley M.: 25 qps sustained on Llama30b hosted is doable with batching but p50 400ms is tight. Need to know sequence lengths (avg / max) and whether KV-cache reuse across requests is high. Also: what quantization are they expecting? int8/4?

Aisha K.: Seq len avg ~ 120 tokens, max ~ 1024. KV reuse pretty high (many short followups per conversation). They prefer int8 for cost, but can accept int4 if quality drop is acceptable.

Jordan S.: Ok — simplified compatibility checklist for this prospect: 
- Tokenizer: standard llama-tokenizer -> compatible.
- Model artifacts: check HF-style weights + config for attention layer naming (need to match runtime loader).
- KV cache layout: confirm transformer cache_key/val shapes (we can adapt a shim but prefer native).
- Quantization: run a quick int8 accuracy sweep on canonical eval set.
- Deployment path: hosted -> dedicated -> private (if KMS/PHI).

Jordan S.: Quick command I can run if someone uploads a sample model manifest (or link to S3):
```
redwood-cli model inspect --manifest s3://pavo-artifacts/llama30b-ft/manifest.json
redwood-ops run-compatibility --model-id pavo-llama30b-ft --checks kv-layout,attention-names,tokenizer
```

Tom L.: For pricing sketch: assume hosted with int8 -> unit tokens cost ~ $0.0009 / 1k tokens (placeholder) + reserved throughput for bursts (if they want <400ms we may need reserved capacity). I'll draft a two-line estimate once we confirm avg token output per request.

Riley M.: Two more ops notes: 1) warm KV-cache hits will drop p50 significantly; we should recommend a short warmup route during POC. 2) If they go int4, we should flag potential hallucination/regression risk and tie to eval sets.

Aisha K.: I'll ask Pavo for sample traffic & a small eval prompt set (15 prompts) — will push to the shared S3. Also they sent a security questionnaire — wondering if we can answer KMS + data retention + model artifact provenance quickly.

legal-bot: Security Qs -> please use https://redwood.internal/legal/sq-template and attach answers there. Short answers we can reuse: "KMS integrated (AWS KMS / customer-managed), data retention configurable per-customer, model provenance logged in ingestion metadata." I'll link a prefilled draft once done.

Jordan S.: I'll take the compatibility run once Aisha posts the manifest. If we see attention-name mismatches we can add a small shim to the loader (low effort). For KV-cache warmup we can provide a pre-signed warmup endpoint pattern and a sample curl to prime cache.

Jordan S.: Example warmup curl: `curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/warmup -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"session_id":"pavo-test","prompts":["hi","followup q1","followup q2"]}'`

Tom L.: I'll attach a pricing sketch after Aisha posts sample average output tokens. For now, rough monthly cost estimate for POC (25qps, int8 hosted, 30-day): ~$18k (compute) + $2k support. Marking as placeholder.

Aisha K.: Uploaded sample manifest + 15 eval prompts to s3://pavo-poc/2026-03-evals. Also added security questionnaire PDF to the same bucket.

Riley M.: Kicked off local int8 sweep against the eval set. Early note: latency P50 at 25qps with batching looks ~380ms but p95 spikes to ~1.1s on cold shards. Warmup should fix most of that.

Jordan S.: Ran the `run-compatibility` job: tokenizer + attention names OK, small kv-shape mismatch on one layer but loader shim passed tests. Tagging results: https://redwood.internal/jobs/COMP-7765 (internal).

legal-bot: Draft sq answers uploaded: https://redwood.internal/legal/drafts/pavo-7765432109-sq. Highlights: KMS integration ok, retention policy: default 30 days (adjustable), audit logs available.

Tom L.: Updated the sketch: POC hosted int8 estimate now $14k/mo (because actual avg output tokens lower than initial guess). If they require SLA <400ms p50 under burst -> recommend Dedicated reserve estimate $28k/mo + onetime setup.

Aisha K.: Great — I'll sync with Pavo tomorrow and confirm whether they want hosted trial or go straight to Dedicated. Can we set a quick call w/ Jordan + Tom? 10am PT tomorrow works.

Jordan S.: 10am PT works for me. :thumbsup:

Riley M.: OK. I'll prepare the warmup endpoint example and attach two quick graphs (latency with/without warmup).

Aisha K.: Thanks everyone — closing the loop after call. :raised_hands:
